<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Critical issues require deeper investigation.

Hibernate `@Lob` on PostgreSQL may map `String` fields to OID large objects rather than TEXT. This conflicts with the frozen spec's requirement to avoid PostgreSQL-specific types and use ordinary nullability and length constraints. Assignee and comment body fields lack explicit max lengths, which further violates the spec.

`ddl-auto=none` without migrations is a Major production risk. The application cannot run against an empty PostgreSQL schema. The assignee field should use plain TEXT or VARCHAR instead of `@Lob`, which would eliminate OID read/write complications.

Priority and status enums lack database CHECK constraints despite the frozen spec requiring constrained values. This is a Major or Minor gap.

Title validation accepts whitespace-only input because the implementation uses only @NotNull and @Size. The spec forbids whitespace-only rejection, so this is Non-compliant.

Terminal state transitions correctly return 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION for CLOSED-to-CLOSED updates and TERMINAL_TICKET_CONFLICT for terminal ticket conflicts.

API security is compliant. The build.gradle contains no Spring Security dependency.

The exact entity count of two and the exact endpoint count of six both match the frozen specifications.

PersistenceModelTests and Jackson configuration still need review for OID mapping and Instant serialization. Schema.sql or migration files must also be checked.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Verifying Hibernate 6 and Spring Boot 3 compatibility.

Hibernate 6.2+ PostgreSQL dialect defaults `@Lob` on String to OID-based large objects. This conflicts with frozen specs requiring CLOB materialization. `@JdbcTypeCode` overrides are needed.

Frozen spec section 14 forbids PostgreSQL-specific features; OID-based `@Lob` violates portable TEXT constraints. Assignee and comment body both use `@Lob` without length, forcing OID creation. Title and description correctly omit `@Lob`. H2 maps `@Lob` to CLOB, masking PostgreSQL OID failures in tests.

Test-strategy explicitly warns about this risk.

ddl-auto=none without schema forces production to rely on external schema creation. The implementation plan leaves migrations as an open choice, yet PR-001 requires persistence. Without Flyway or Liquibase, table creation is unguaranteed.

Enum fields use EnumType.STRING without @Column(columnDefinition) or @Check annotations. Hibernate auto-ddl therefore omits database CHECK constraints. The data model mandates constrained textual values, so this is a Major compliance gap.

H2 tests may also lack database CHECK constraints. The data model requires constrained textual values, so this is a Minor compliance gap. Java enums prevent invalid strings at the application level, but native SQL could still bypass database-level enforcement.

GlobalExceptionHandler does not catch all 500 errors. This aligns with the implementation plan’s instruction to avoid inventing behavior.

Request URI extraction excludes query parameters, satisfying the frozen spec.

findAll ordering is not guaranteed, which is acceptable.

The createTicket endpoint explicitly sets status OPEN despite the entity default, but this is harmless.

Empty keyword strings are treated as no restriction in both the service layer and repository, matching the frozen spec. This is COMPLIANT.

listTickets routes null keywords to findAll rather than empty-string queries.

No Spring Security is present. Sensitive values in application.properties are loaded from environment variables, which is sound.

Checking .env.example for committed secrets.
</details></think>
